html:
SMTO-EXE-0167 — SMTO couldn't convert this document

GUID: ad2bf484-c4dd-5b51-a4de-ad99dcbfd55d
Slug: office-conversion-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • A document conversion was reported as failed. SMTO can't convert documents in this version, so no converted file was made, and SMTO never overwrites the original.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that your original document is still where it was and opens normally. SMTO never writes over the original, so it should be unchanged.
  2. Open the document in Word, Excel, PowerPoint or a similar app and use Save As or Export to make the converted copy. SMTO has no safe conversion tool, so converting it yourself is the reliable way.
  3. If you need SMTO to work with the converted copy, attach it with Add context. This gives SMTO the finished file to read or share.

What success looks like

  • You have the converted file from your office app and the original is unchanged.

If it still fails

  • This message shouldn't appear in current versions of SMTO. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO so they can report it. Installing LibreOffice or other apps on the Gateway won't fix it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An office.conversion_failed receipt was reported; this identity is retained for compatibility and has no current producer, because the Office worker rejects convert_to_pdf as conversion_backend_unavailable before attempting any conversion.

What this means

  • A conversion-failed compatibility identity is retained, but the current conversion path rejects unavailable backend support before conversion and has no direct producer for this failure. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • A conversion-failed compatibility identity is retained, but the current conversion path rejects unavailable backend support before conversion and has no direct producer for this failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the historical receipt and current conversion capability; do not invent a running converter or a document-specific cause.

How to fix it

  • Treat the receipt as historical: conversion is not implemented and installing an application does not enable it. Keep the original document, check the selected Gateway's office conversion capability (capabilities operation), and use a separately approved conversion workflow; report a fresh conversion_failed receipt from a current build as a bug.
  • Preserve the original document and inspect current conversion support; installing an application alone does not enable this tool's conversion path.

Retry and execution caution

  • Keep the original file and inspect backend capability before requesting conversion again.

How to verify the fix

  • The original remains preserved and any conversion is handled by a separately supported workflow.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
